name: Tunis
shortDescription: A layered capital where a UNESCO medina, Ottoman palaces and Roman mosaics sit half an hour from the sea.
whyGo: Few capitals pack this much history into short distances. You can spend a morning lost in covered souks, an afternoon among the world's finest Roman mosaics, and end the day watching the sun drop behind Carthage's ruins.
bestTimeToVisit: March to May and September to November, when days are warm and the medina is not baking.
tripDurationSuggestion: 2–3 days, or 4 with Carthage and Sidi Bou Said

neighborhoods.name: Medina of Tunis
neighborhoods.note: Covered souks, tiled palaces and tea rooms behind the Zitouna mosque.

neighborhoods.name: Ville Nouvelle
neighborhoods.note: Wide avenues, art-deco façades and café terraces along Habib Bourguiba.

neighborhoods.name: Carthage
neighborhoods.note: Seaside archaeological sites spread over a quiet residential hill.

neighborhoods.name: La Marsa
neighborhoods.note: Beach promenade where Tunis goes to eat ice cream at sunset.

thingsToDo: Walk the medina from Bab Bhar to the Zitouna mosque early, before the souks fill
Give the Bardo Museum a slow two hours for its Roman mosaic halls
Climb to a rooftop terrace above the souks for the whole medina at once
Take the TGM train along the coast to the Carthage ruins

localFood.name: Lablabi
localFood.note: Chickpea soup over torn bread, eaten standing at breakfast counters.

localFood.name: Brik à l'oeuf
localFood.note: Thin pastry folded around egg and tuna, fried to order.

localFood.name: Ojja merguez
localFood.note: Eggs poached in spiced tomato with lamb sausage.

localFood.name: Makroudh
localFood.note: Semolina pastry filled with dates, soaked in honey.

travelTips: Fridays quieten the souks around midday prayer — plan museums then
Agree a louage or taxi fare before setting off; meters are often 'broken'
Cash still rules in the medina; cards work in the Ville Nouvelle
Say 'la, shukran' politely and keep walking if a guide attaches himself to you

name: Sidi Bou Said
shortDescription: A blue-and-white village on a cliff above the Gulf of Tunis, best walked in the late afternoon.
whyGo: It is small enough to see in an afternoon and beautiful enough to stay until dark: cobbled lanes, studded blue doors, bougainvillea, and a café terrace looking straight down at the marina.
bestTimeToVisit: April to June, or September, when the light is soft and the lanes are not crowded.
tripDurationSuggestion: Half a day, or one night to have the village at dawn
heroImageQuery: Sidi Bou Said blue white village Tunisia
galleryImageQueries: Sidi Bou Said blue door detail
Sidi Bou Said cafe terrace sea

neighborhoods.name: Main lane
neighborhoods.note: The climb from the entrance to the lighthouse, lined with craft shops.

neighborhoods.name: Marina side
neighborhoods.note: Steps down to the port, quieter and good for sunset.

thingsToDo: Climb the main lane to the lighthouse before the tour groups arrive
Drink a mint tea with pine nuts on a terrace above the gulf
Visit Dar el Annabi for a look inside a traditional family house
Walk down to the marina for the view back up at the cliff

localFood.name: Bambalouni
localFood.note: Hot sugared doughnut sold from a hatch near the entrance.

localFood.name: Thé aux pignons
localFood.note: Sweet mint tea crowded with toasted pine nuts.

localFood.name: Grilled sea bream
localFood.note: Straight off the boats at the marina restaurants.

travelTips: Arrive after 16:00 for light and space; midday is the busiest hour
The TGM train from Tunis is cheap and drops you a short walk below the village
Cobbles and a steady climb — flat shoes beat sandals here
Most cafés are cash only

name: Paris
shortDescription: Grand boulevards and small neighbourhoods — the city rewards walking one arrondissement at a time.
whyGo: Paris works best when you stop trying to see all of it. Pick two neighbourhoods a day, eat where the queue is local, and let the landmarks appear between them.
bestTimeToVisit: Late April to June and September to October — long light, gardens open, fewer closures than August.

neighborhoods.name: Le Marais
neighborhoods.note: Narrow streets, falafel counters, small museums in old mansions.

neighborhoods.name: Saint-Germain-des-Prés
neighborhoods.note: Literary cafés, galleries and the Luxembourg gardens.

neighborhoods.name: Canal Saint-Martin
neighborhoods.note: Iron footbridges, natural wine bars, younger crowd.

neighborhoods.name: Montmartre
neighborhoods.note: Steep lanes and village feel above the tourist steps.

thingsToDo: Walk the Seine between Pont Neuf and Île Saint-Louis in the early evening
Take the Musée d'Orsay over the Louvre if you have one museum in you
Buy lunch at a market street — Rue Mouffetard or Rue des Martyrs
Sit in the Luxembourg gardens with a pastry and no plan

localFood.name: Jambon-beurre
localFood.note: Ham and butter on a fresh baguette — the honest Paris lunch.

localFood.name: Steak frites
localFood.note: Bistro standard; order it rarer than you think.

localFood.name: Pain au chocolat
localFood.note: Judge a bakery by its lamination, not its queue.

localFood.name: Natural wine
localFood.note: Canal Saint-Martin and the 11th pour the interesting bottles.

travelTips: Many museums close Mondays or Tuesdays — check before you build a day around one
A carnet of metro tickets or a Navigo Easy card beats buying singles
Bakeries close one day a week, often Sunday or Monday
Reserve dinner for 19:30 or 21:30; 20:30 is when everyone else calls

name: Rome
shortDescription: Twenty-eight centuries stacked on one another, with dinner in the middle of it.
whyGo: Rome is the rare city where the ruins are not fenced off from daily life — you cross a Roman road on the way to lunch, and the best square is the one you stumble into after dark.
bestTimeToVisit: April to early June and late September to October; August is hot and half-shuttered.

neighborhoods.name: Trastevere
neighborhoods.note: Ivy, cobbles and trattorias across the river.

neighborhoods.name: Monti
neighborhoods.note: Vintage shops and wine bars a few steps from the Forum.

neighborhoods.name: Testaccio
neighborhoods.note: Market quarter where Roman food traditions are strongest.

neighborhoods.name: Centro Storico
neighborhoods.note: Pantheon, piazzas and the crowds that come with them.

thingsToDo: See the Forum and Palatine first thing, then the Colosseum after
Eat where Testaccio's market traders eat, not where the menus have photos
Walk the Appian Way on a Sunday when it closes to traffic
Stand under the Pantheon's oculus in light rain if you get the chance

localFood.name: Cacio e pepe
localFood.note: Three ingredients, nowhere to hide — the local test of a kitchen.

localFood.name: Supplì
localFood.note: Fried rice ball with a molten mozzarella centre.

localFood.name: Carciofi alla giudia
localFood.note: Flattened, deep-fried artichoke from the Jewish quarter.

localFood.name: Maritozzo
localFood.note: Sweet bun split and filled with cream, eaten at breakfast.

travelTips: Book Colosseum and Vatican slots ahead; walk-ups burn hours
Cover shoulders and knees for churches, including small ones
Drink from the nasoni street fountains — the water is excellent
Sitting down costs more than standing at the bar for coffee

name: Istanbul
shortDescription: Two continents, one ferry ride, and a food scene that rewards eating five small things instead of one big one.
whyGo: Istanbul is best understood from the water: the skyline changes every few minutes, and each shore has its own pace — imperial on one side, neighbourhood cafés and markets on the other.
bestTimeToVisit: April to May and September to November — mild, clear and good for walking.

neighborhoods.name: Sultanahmet
neighborhoods.note: The imperial core: Hagia Sophia, Blue Mosque, Topkapı.

neighborhoods.name: Karaköy & Galata
neighborhoods.note: Coffee, design shops and the tower, steeply uphill.

neighborhoods.name: Kadıköy
neighborhoods.note: Asian-side market streets where locals actually eat.

neighborhoods.name: Balat
neighborhoods.note: Coloured houses, antique shops, quiet lanes.

thingsToDo: Cross to Kadıköy by public ferry and eat your way through the market
See Hagia Sophia early, then the Basilica Cistern when the sun is high
Walk Balat's lanes with no route in mind
Have a long Turkish breakfast on a weekend — it is the main event

localFood.name: Balık ekmek
localFood.note: Grilled fish in bread, eaten by the Galata bridge.

localFood.name: Menemen
localFood.note: Soft eggs with tomato and green pepper, scooped with bread.

localFood.name: Lahmacun
localFood.note: Thin flatbread with minced lamb — squeeze lemon, roll, eat.

localFood.name: Künefe
localFood.note: Shredded pastry over melting cheese in syrup.

travelTips: An Istanbulkart covers ferries, trams and buses — buy one on arrival
Ferries are transport, not tours, and cost a fraction of cruise prices
Carry a scarf for mosque visits and slip-on shoes for the shoe racks
Traffic is the real distance; plan by ferry and tram, not by map line

name: Tokyo
shortDescription: A city of villages under neon — quiet shrines and standing noodle bars a minute apart.
whyGo: Tokyo rewards curiosity at small scale: a six-seat counter, a basement record shop, a shrine between office towers. Pick a station, walk out, and the city does the rest.
bestTimeToVisit: Late March to April for blossom, or October to November for clear, cool days.

neighborhoods.name: Shibuya & Shimokitazawa
neighborhoods.note: Crossings and crowds, then thrift shops and coffee two stops away.

neighborhoods.name: Asakusa & Yanaka
neighborhoods.note: Old-Tokyo lanes, temples and sweet shops.

neighborhoods.name: Shinjuku
neighborhoods.note: Department-store basements, tiny bars in Golden Gai.

neighborhoods.name: Nakameguro
neighborhoods.note: Canal-side walking, small design shops.

thingsToDo: Eat standing at a station soba counter during the morning rush
Walk Yanaka's lanes and its cemetery avenue in the late afternoon
Spend an hour in a department-store food hall before dinner
Ride the Yamanote line one full loop when you are tired

localFood.name: Tsukemen
localFood.note: Cold noodles dipped into concentrated hot broth.

localFood.name: Onigiri
localFood.note: Rice triangles done seriously — convenience stores included.

localFood.name: Yakitori
localFood.note: Charcoal skewers under railway arches, ordered one at a time.

localFood.name: Melonpan
localFood.note: Crisp-topped sweet bun, best straight from the oven.

travelTips: Get a Suica or Pasmo card; most small places still prefer cash
Trains stop around midnight — plan the last leg before dinner
Queues move fast and are a good sign, not a warning
Carry your rubbish; public bins are rare

name: Marrakech
shortDescription: Souks, courtyards and roof terraces, with the Atlas mountains on the horizon.
whyGo: The medina is loud, bright and relentless — and then you step through a plain door into a cool tiled courtyard and the city makes sense. The contrast is the whole appeal.
bestTimeToVisit: March to May and October to November; summer regularly passes 40°C.
tripDurationSuggestion: 3 days, plus one for the Atlas or Essaouira

neighborhoods.name: Medina
neighborhoods.note: Souks, riads and the main square, all on foot.

neighborhoods.name: Kasbah
neighborhoods.note: Quieter southern quarter near the Saadian tombs.

neighborhoods.name: Gueliz
neighborhoods.note: Modern grid with galleries, cafés and wine lists.

neighborhoods.name: Palmeraie
neighborhoods.note: Palm groves and pools outside the walls.

thingsToDo: Get lost in the souks on purpose, then hire a guide for the second day
See Ben Youssef Madrasa when it opens and have the courtyard to yourself
Watch Jemaa el-Fnaa fill from a terrace at dusk
Take a half-day into the Atlas foothills for cooler air

localFood.name: Tanjia
localFood.note: Marrakech's own slow-cooked lamb, sealed in a clay urn.

localFood.name: Harira
localFood.note: Tomato and lentil soup, often with dates on the side.

localFood.name: Msemen
localFood.note: Flaky square pancake with honey, for breakfast.

localFood.name: Mint tea
localFood.note: Poured high; sweet by default, ask for less sugar.

travelTips: Agree prices before anything — a tea, a taxi, a 'shortcut' guide
Riads are cooler and quieter than hotels on the ring road
Fridays are slower; couscous is the traditional family lunch
Carry small notes; change is a constant negotiation

name: Bali
shortDescription: Rice terraces, temple mornings and surf afternoons — pick one or two bases, not five.
whyGo: Bali is several islands in temperament: highland villages with cool evenings, a surf coast, and quiet east-side beaches. The trick is choosing two and travelling slowly between them.
bestTimeToVisit: May to September is drier; April and October are quieter with a little rain.

neighborhoods.name: Ubud
neighborhoods.note: Rice fields, craft villages, cool evenings inland.

neighborhoods.name: Canggu
neighborhoods.note: Surf breaks, cafés, motorbike traffic.

neighborhoods.name: Uluwatu
neighborhoods.note: Cliffs, big swell, sunset temple.

neighborhoods.name: Amed & the east
neighborhoods.note: Black-sand bays, snorkelling, very quiet.

thingsToDo: Walk the Campuhan ridge before breakfast while it is still cool
Eat at a warung where the plate is assembled in front of you
Snorkel the eastern bays instead of joining a boat crowd
Take a morning temple visit seriously — dress and behave as a guest

localFood.name: Nasi campur
localFood.note: Rice with a rotating handful of small dishes.

localFood.name: Babi guling
localFood.note: Spit-roast pork, a Balinese celebration dish.

localFood.name: Sate lilit
localFood.note: Minced fish satay wrapped on lemongrass.

localFood.name: Kopi tubruk
localFood.note: Strong unfiltered coffee; let the grounds settle.

travelTips: Distances look short and take hours — build in transfer time
A sarong is required at temples; most lend them at the gate
Rent a scooter only with the right licence and a real helmet
Carry cash for warungs; card acceptance is patchy outside tourist strips
